title: Define model comparison study success criteria
description: Before the study ends, agree on what 'winning' looks like. Number of games? Average fun score? Playtest time? Write it down so we judge fairly.
notes: Probably a simple rubric: visual quality, gameplay fun, stability, replay value. Rate 1-5 per category per game.

title: Decide on quality gate thresholds for hard checks
description: What does a game need to do to pass a hard gate? Runs without crash, has a score, has a lose condition, loads in < 5s. Define this before building the gate system.
notes: Keep hard gates binary — pass or fail. Soft rubric handles subjective quality.

title: Write retrospective after model comparison study
description: Document what we learned about Claude vs Codex for game generation. What surprised us? What held up? What do we change in the skill?
notes: Do this after the study is done, not during.

title: Investigate parallel multi-agent game generation
description: Is it worth splitting game generation across agents? Logic agent + visual agent + balance agent. Would need conflict resolution strategy for shared files.
notes: High complexity. Only worth exploring after the single-agent study shows clear ceiling.

title: Plan community game submission pipeline
description: If we open to community games, we need a review process, format spec, and quality bar. What makes a community game different from an agent game?
notes: Not urgent. Revisit after the study and quality gate work is done.
